data.note:
Missed DNA replication (camptothecin) as Microtubule stabilizers.

True MoA: camptothecin traps topoisomerase I-DNA cleavage complexes blocking replication, reviewed in PMID:16990856; also topoisomerase inhibitor class PMID:8305535 and PMID:2557085.

Why I was misled: bright condensed tubulin/actin (tub_mean z~+19-28, act_std z up to +69), small irregular nuclei, rounded contracted cells and reduced counts look like stabilized microtubules/mitotic arrest, and atlas 8/10 neighbours were stabilizers with NSC 2/4.

What should have warned me: similarities were weak 0.44-0.68, per-well NSC split 3 classes (stabilizer / protein synthesis / cholesterol-lowering), Microscopists disagreed (actin disruptor vs stabilizer), replicate at 10uM disagreed on frac_mitotic_like +17.9 vs -0.2, and tub_mean was flat with dose rho=0.11. That pattern is secondary cytoskeletal condensation/apoptotic nuclear fragmentation downstream of replication stress, not primary tubulin stabilization. Small nuc_area z~-24, form_factor z~-42/-71 and solidity loss fit fragmented/condensed nuclei.

Lesson: require dose-dependent mitotic signature and high similarity before voting rare cytoskeletal class; when votes split and replicates disagree, favour DNA replication/damage explanation and check phospho-H3/DNA-content and tubulin polymerization assay.

reflection.text:
The run concluded Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.72, but unblinding revealed camptothecin, truth DNA replication / topoisomerase I inhibition. The error was over-weighting extreme high-dose texture features and an NSC neighbour majority while under-weighting inconsistent per-well votes and non-significant dose-response.

What misled was acquisition and comparison choice: two of four wells were the same 10 uM high dose with extreme act_std z=+69.0, nuc_form_factor z=-42.4 to -71.0 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+26.9 to +29.5, and NSC 8/10 neighbours voted stabilizers. The split signal was visible — 0.3 uM voted Protein synthesis (similarity 0.439) and 1 uM voted Cholesterol-lowering (0.469), and tub_mean rho=+0.11 p=0.89 and frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.63 p=0.37 were non-significant — but I treated rounding and tubulin masses on second visual as confirmatory.

In retrospect the low cell counts (56-94 cells), lower density, reduced nuc_area z=-24.4 and very irregular nuclei were compatible with secondary mitotic / nuclear disruption from DNA replication stress rather than direct stabilization. DNA replication was not retained as a hypothesis, so no discriminating S-phase versus mitotic test was done.
what_was_right: Detected a potent anti-proliferative phenotype with lower density vs DMSO and low counts at 1-10 uM (56-94 cells) plus shrunken irregular nuclei (nuc_area z=-24.4, nuc_form_factor z=-42.4 to -71.0, nuc_solidity z=-43.2).
Recorded that evidence was split: per-well NSC votes differed by dose and dose-response tests were non-significant (frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.63 p=0.37; tub_mean rho=+0.11 p=0.89).
Kept Actin disruptors as an alternative after the first microscopist call of Actin disruptors, recognizing actin/tubulin texture extremes alone were ambiguous.
what_was_wrong: Interpreted high-dose act_std, act_glcm_contrast and tub_glcm_contrast extremes and rounding as direct microtubule stabilization, missing that topoisomerase I-mediated DNA replication stress can produce secondary mitotic-like rounding and cytoskeletal texture changes.

Over-relied on NSC 2/4 majority and 8/10 k-neighbour tally driven by two 10 uM replicates (similarities 0.562 and 0.678) while discounting divergent 0.3 uM Protein synthesis and 1 uM Cholesterol-lowering votes.
Treated non-significant dose-response trends as supportive of stabilizers and submitted without including or testing a DNA replication / DNA damage hypothesis.

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Steps

1. `list_available_experiments` — Need dose list and budget to plan discriminating wells.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 12: Microtubule stabilizers 0.72, Actin disruptors 0.12, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.05, Protein synthesis 0.04, Microtubule destabilizers 0.04, Cholesterol-lowering 0.03

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.72); key evidence e8, e9, e2, e6, e10.

Why: NSC 2/4 and 8/10 neighbours favor stabilizers; imaging confirms tubulin masses and rounding.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Phospho-histone H3 + DNA content flow cytometry for G2/M arrest and in vitro tubulin polymerization assay to confirm stabilization vs actin effect.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean profile, no unsupported chemical identity asserted. Direct morphological reasoning distinguishing possibility from indication.

## Unblinding

Compound: **camptothecin** (PubChem CID [24360](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/24360))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

## Reflection

The run concluded Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.72, but unblinding revealed camptothecin, truth DNA replication / topoisomerase I inhibition. The error was over-weighting extreme high-dose texture features and an NSC neighbour majority while under-weighting inconsistent per-well votes and non-significant dose-response.

What misled was acquisition and comparison choice: two of four wells were the same 10 uM high dose with extreme act_std z=+69.0, nuc_form_factor z=-42.4 to -71.0 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+26.9 to +29.5, and NSC 8/10 neighbours voted stabilizers. The split signal was visible — 0.3 uM voted Protein synthesis (similarity 0.439) and 1 uM voted Cholesterol-lowering (0.469), and tub_mean rho=+0.11 p=0.89 and frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.63 p=0.37 were non-significant — but I treated rounding and tubulin masses on second visual as confirmatory.

In retrospect the low cell counts (56-94 cells), lower density, reduced nuc_area z=-24.4 and very irregular nuclei were compatible with secondary mitotic / nuclear disruption from DNA replication stress rather than direct stabilization. DNA replication was not retained as a hypothesis, so no discriminating S-phase versus mitotic test was done.

What was right:
- Detected a potent anti-proliferative phenotype with lower density vs DMSO and low counts at 1-10 uM (56-94 cells) plus shrunken irregular nuclei (nuc_area z=-24.4, nuc_form_factor z=-42.4 to -71.0, nuc_solidity z=-43.2).
- Recorded that evidence was split: per-well NSC votes differed by dose and dose-response tests were non-significant (frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.63 p=0.37; tub_mean rho=+0.11 p=0.89).
- Kept Actin disruptors as an alternative after the first microscopist call of Actin disruptors, recognizing actin/tubulin texture extremes alone were ambiguous.

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted high-dose act_std, act_glcm_contrast and tub_glcm_contrast extremes and rounding as direct microtubule stabilization, missing that topoisomerase I-mediated DNA replication stress can produce secondary mitotic-like rounding and cytoskeletal texture changes.
- Over-relied on NSC 2/4 majority and 8/10 k-neighbour tally driven by two 10 uM replicates (similarities 0.562 and 0.678) while discounting divergent 0.3 uM Protein synthesis and 1 uM Cholesterol-lowering votes.
- Treated non-significant dose-response trends as supportive of stabilizers and submitted without including or testing a DNA replication / DNA damage hypothesis.

Proposed next experiment: EdU incorporation plus gamma-H2AX and DNA-content cell-cycle profiling for S-phase DNA replication stress versus G2/M arrest, with a cell-free tubulin polymerization assay and a stabilizer control to test direct microtubule stabilization.

- PMID [8305535](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8305535/): DNA-topoisomerase inhibitors. *Curr Opin Oncol* (1993) — DNA-topoisomerase inhibitors are a recognized class of oncology drugs.
- PMID [2557085](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2557085/): Topoisomerase-targeting antitumor drugs. *Biochim Biophys Acta* (1989) — Topoisomerase-targeting drugs have antitumor activity.
- PMID [36114357](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36114357/): Mechanism of action of non-camptothecin inhibitor Genz-644282 in topoisomerase I inhibition. *Commun Biol* (2022) — Topoisomerase I can also be inhibited by non-camptothecin mechanisms as shown for Genz-644282.
